source_review: DataStorage.prepareVolume calls getBlockPoolSliceStorage(nsInfo), which inserts the block-pool ID into bpStorageMap if absent, then adds that ID to VolumeBuilder.bpStorageDirMap (DataStorage.java:324-348,1409-1418). VolumeBuilder.build checks the same map under synchronized(storage) (DataStorage.java:251-263). The only map removal is removeBlockPoolStorage from DataNode.shutdownBlockPool after BPOfferService removes its last actor (DataStorage.java:1421-1423; DataNode.java:2147-2165; BPOfferService.java:465-479). The original one-NN/one-DN volume-add JUnit does not intentionally shut down that block pool. An IPC fault could still indirectly alter actor lifetime, so the 80 target-retaining trials give bounded evidence, not a proof of impossibility. File I/O exceptions in prepareVolume normally abort before build and were outside this case's RPC response injection scope.
depth_three_note: 20 three-fault attempts, 18 strict; none retained the selected target. The 80 target-retaining trials comprise 10 one-fault and 70 two-fault sequences.
